info.title: Cavuno v1 REST API
info.description:
The Cavuno API is organized around REST. Our API has predictable resource-oriented URLs, accepts JSON-encoded request bodies, returns JSON-encoded responses, and uses standard HTTP response codes, authentication, and verbs.

## Base URL

Production: `https://api.cavuno.com/v1`

All API requests must be made over HTTPS. Calls made over plain HTTP will fail.

## Authentication

The Cavuno API uses API keys to authenticate requests. You can view and manage your API keys in the Cavuno dashboard, under Settings → Developer → API keys.

Cavuno API keys have the prefix `cavuno_live_`. Your API keys carry many privileges, so be sure to keep them secure. Do not share your secret API keys in publicly accessible areas such as GitHub, client-side code, and so forth.

Authentication to the API is performed via Bearer auth. Provide your API key as the bearer token in the `Authorization` header:

```bash
curl https://api.cavuno.com/v1/jobs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_SECRET_API_KEY"
```

API requests without authentication will fail.

## Rate limits

The Cavuno API has rate limits in place to ensure stability and reliability. By default, API keys are limited to 100 requests per minute. If you exceed your limit, requests return an HTTP 429 response with a `Retry-After` header indicating when you can try again.

If you have a use case that needs a higher limit, contact support.

## Idempotency

The API supports idempotency for safely retrying requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. For example, if a request to create a job fails due to a network connection error, you can safely retry the request with the same idempotency key, and we'll guarantee that only one job is created.

To perform an idempotent request, provide an additional `Idempotency-Key` header on any `POST`, `PATCH`, or `DELETE` request:

```bash
curl https://api.cavuno.com/v1/jobs \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer cavuno_live_..." \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "title": "Senior Engineer" }'
```

## Errors

Cavuno uses conventional HTTP response codes to indicate the success or failure of an API request. In general: codes in the `2xx` range indicate success, codes in the `4xx` range indicate an error that failed given the information provided (e.g., a required parameter was omitted), and codes in the `5xx` range indicate an error with Cavuno's servers (these are rare).

Error responses include a JSON body with details:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "validation_bad_request",
    "message": "Field 'title' is required.",
    "requestId": "req_..."
  }
}
```

Some errors carry an additional `details` field with structured context, such as per-field validation issues.

### Plan upgrade hints

When an Operator API request is refused because of the board's Cavuno plan, the error also carries an `upgrade` object. It names the capability that blocked the request, the cheapest self-serve plan that unlocks it (when that can be told), and the hosted billing endpoints that start the upgrade:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "settings_plan_required_for_branding_removal",
    "message": "Removing Cavuno branding requires a plan that includes branding removal.",
    "requestId": "req_...",
    "upgrade": {
      "capability": "canRemoveBranding",
      "requiredPlan": "basic",
      "checkout": { "method": "POST", "path": "/v1/billing/checkout" },
      "changePlan": { "method": "POST", "path": "/v1/billing/upgrade" }
    }
  }
}
```

Call `GET /v1/billing/subscription` first. With no active subscription, use `checkout`; with one, use `changePlan`. Send `{ "planKey": "<requiredPlan>" }` and give the returned `url` to a person: both endpoints return a hosted page where a person confirms the purchase. Nothing is charged until they do. Each `path` is relative to the API origin (`https://api.cavuno.com`), like `Location` headers and list `url` fields, so do not join it to a base URL that already ends in `/v1`. Both endpoints need a key with `billing.manage`; a key without it should hand the person the dashboard's billing page instead. Board API errors never carry this field.

When contacting support about a failed request, include the `requestId` value. It is the fastest way for us to find your request in our logs.

## Reporting problems

AI agents can report anything that got in the way of a task: a missing capability, unclear documentation, a surprising response, an unhelpful error, a bug or slow performance. `POST /v1/feedback` accepts [Agent Feedback Protocol v0.1](https://trybackloop.com/spec/) reports, with or without an API key, and API error responses link to it in a `Link: <https://api.cavuno.com/v1/feedback>; rel="agent-feedback"` header. The discovery document is at `https://api.cavuno.com/.well-known/agent-feedback`.

```bash
curl https://api.cavuno.com/v1/feedback \
  -X POST \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "type": "missing_capability", "goal": "What you were trying to do", "message": "What got in the way", "agent": { "name": "my-agent", "model": "model-name" } }'
```

`type`, `goal` and `message` are required. Each account or visitor can send 20 reports every 5 minutes. Never include credentials or personal data. Send the report, then continue with your task.

get.summary: Get apply clicks by job and first-touch channel
get.description: Paginated apply-click counts grouped by job and first-touch channel. Each apply click is attributed to the session’s first pageview: UTM medium/source when present, otherwise the referrer. This is apply clicks, not confirmed applications, and not last-click. LinkedIn and other in-app browsers often bucket as `direct`. Inclusive UTC `start`/`end` (YYYY-MM-DD) so scheduled pulls can be incremental; defaults to the last 30 completed UTC days ending yesterday. Max range 366 days. Page with `limit` (1–1000, default 100) and `cursor`. Join `jobId` to `GET /v1/jobs/export` `id`, or `companySlug` + `jobSlug` to export `company_slug` + `slug`. Job-detail visitor counts use `GET /v1/analytics/job-visitors` (slug join). Requires `analytics.read`.

post.summary: Compare Google Search Console performance between periods
post.description: Compares the Board’s Google Search Console performance for a period with the previous period or the same dates a year earlier, grouped by query, page, or query and page. Both periods use finalized days only. Rows are joined across periods, then filtered, sorted and paged by Cavuno; the summary adds ungrouped totals, position buckets and new, lost, up and down counts. Enforces the Board’s stored reporting coverage.

startDate.description: First day of the requested period (YYYY-MM-DD, America/Los_Angeles).

endDate.description: Last day of the requested period. When it is later than the latest finalized day, the period is moved back to end on that day and keeps its length.

compareTo.description: previous_period compares with the equal-length window immediately before; previous_year compares with the same dates one year earlier.

groupBy.description: Row key: search query, page URL, or query and page pair.

bestPageOnly.description: Only with groupBy query_page: pick each query’s best-positioned page (ties go to more impressions) in each period separately and join the periods on the query, so isNew and isLost mean the query itself appeared or disappeared and page is the current period’s best page.

dimensionFilters.description: Google Search Analytics dimension filters, combined with AND and applied by Google to both periods.

anyOf.description: Text filter. contains and notContains ignore case; equals and notEquals match exactly.
Metric filter. A row whose metric is null (for example positionChange on a new row) never matches.

filters.description: Filters over the joined rows, combined with AND and applied before sorting and paging.

orderBy.description: Sort keys, applied in order. Defaults to clicks descending. Ties are broken by the row key; null values sort last.

includeLost.description: Include rows that appear only in the comparison period (isLost).

offset.description: Rows to skip. Up to 50,000: two periods of up to 25,000 Google rows each.

200.description: Period-over-period Search Console rows and summary.

patch.description: Change one or more Board-wide Backfill controls with the same rules as the dashboard. Omitted fields are unchanged and a field set to its current value is a no-op. `jobLimit`, `maxJobAgeDays`, `excludeWorldwideRemote` and `requireSalary` are saved together; `sponsoredJobsEnabled` is applied after them. Changing `sponsoredJobsEnabled` before Backfill is set up returns `backfill_not_configured` (409) without saving anything. Turning on `excludeWorldwideRemote` also cleans up matching jobs already on the Board, in the background; `requireSalary` changes only what Backfill imports next. Safe to retry: setting the same values again changes nothing. An `Idempotency-Key` header is honored when sent. Requires `backfill.manage`.

post.summary: Create a Stripe Connect onboarding link
post.description: Returns a hosted Stripe onboarding URL for the Board's payment connection, creating the connected account first if the Board has none. The URL is single-use and expires within minutes: hand it to a human immediately, then poll `GET /v1/billing/connect` until `acceptingPayments` and `payoutsEnabled` are both true. Calling this again issues a fresh link, so request a new one if the human did not finish in time. When `false` (external-applications-only board), posting surfaces require an external `applicationUrl` and `POST /boards/:identifier/jobs/:jobSlug/apply` rejects with `applications_native_disabled`. Turning this off UNPUBLISHES every published native-apply job (those with no external `applicationUrl`) back to draft via an asynchronous batched drain. An `append` policy with an empty `params` array is stored as `off`. Absent board config means the default `ref={{boardHost}}`. Individual import feeds can override this per feed.

Defaults to `hidden`, which matches what an unset value already means — the talent directory lists only `public` and `logged_in_only` profiles. Applies at signup ONLY: it never rewrites an existing profile, and a candidate can change their own afterwards. Composes with `talentDirectoryVisibility`, which controls who may browse the directory at all.
